US signals progress in Iran talks to avert flare-up. US President Donald Trump signaled progress on Tuesday in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war , as Tehran reported “intensive” exchanges while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions. The fresh diplomatic signals came ahead of US midterm elections on Tuesday, in which Trump’s Republican Party is pushing to retain control of Congress, faced with voter dissatisfaction over the conflict and the soaring fuel prices it has triggered. A deal with Tehran “could happen,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible.” But hours later, Washington’s diplomatic overtures were dashed by a report that the United States had attacked Iran, in what the Wall Street Journal said was the latest in a string of limited strikes it secretly carried out against the Islamic republic in recent weeks. Iranian state media reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz. The US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment. Earlier, oil prices plunged by more than seven per cent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict. The WSJ report came shortly before polls opened in the midterms, in which Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years. Reopen the strait Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect talks with Washington were taking place via mediators. “Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi told state media. “Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations.” Vice President JD Vance said both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday. China also urged a return to diplomacy , while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Earlier, the Axios news outlet reported that Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months. Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from Washington were “an acknowledgement of our victory.” A senior Iranian official said that Tehran was ready to open the Hormuz strait, an export conduit for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days — as long as Washington agreed to its list of demands. In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait, with demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports. “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” Tehran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing. Chinese President Xi Jinping also discussed the war with Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing on Monday – the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established. “The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” an Omani statement said. ‘No compromises’ China held meetings with Iranian and Saudi officials in Beijing on Monday as well. Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security,” Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement. Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard,” state TV reported. In an interview with Al Jazeer a released on Sunday, Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait. He said Washington must also remove sanctions imposed recently and reduce American troop numbers in the region. Trump has kept up his threats against Tehran, saying on Sunday that the United States may have to give Iran “ the hammer ” at some unspecified time. On Saturday, the US leader said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. Baqaei warned that any act of aggression against Iran “will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response. “

Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz named in Pakistan Shaheens squad for Rising Stars Asia Cup. Maaz Sadaqat and Hasan Nawaz have been included in the 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, with Abdul Samad appointed captain for the 50-over tournament to be held in Qatar from Nov 19 to 29. The Pakistan Cricket Board announced the squad on Tuesday, with the Shaheens set to defend the title they won in the previous 50-over edition in 2023. Pakistan are also the defending champions of the T20 version of the competition, having beaten Bangladesh A in a final decided by a Super Over. The eight-team tournament will feature two groups of four sides. Pakistan have been placed in Group ‘B’ alongside India A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates, while Group ‘A’ comprises Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China and Sri Lanka A. The Shaheens will open their campaign against the UAE on Nov 20, before taking on India A two days later and Nepal on Nov 24. Their first match will be played at the University of Doha Science and Technology ground, with the remaining group fixtures scheduled at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium. All three group matches are day-night fixtures except the opening game, which will be played during the day. The semi-finals are scheduled for Nov 26 and 27, with the final to be held on Nov 29. Samad will lead a batting group that includes Maaz, Hasan, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf and Shamyl Hussain. Rohail Nazir has been named as the designated wicket-keeper. The squad also includes three spin options in left-arm spin all-rounder Danish Aziz, leg-spinner Saad Masood and Sufyan Moqim. The pace attack will be led by Mohammad Hasnain and also features Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed and Muhammad Imran Randhawa. Ahmed Daniyal was part of the Shaheens side that won the previous T20 edition, playing a key role as the team clinched the title against Bangladesh A in a Super Over. Pakistan won the last 50-over edition in Sri Lanka in 2023, beating India A by 128 runs in the final. They were runners-up in the opening two editions in 2013 and 2017 before winning the competition in 2019. The Shaheens will be aiming to retain their title against a field that includes several of the region’s emerging sides, with a meeting against India A among the key fixtures in the group stage.

Australia's Glenn Maxwell calls time on international career. Explosive batsman Glenn Maxwell announced his international retirement Tuesday after being overlooked for Australia’s upcoming Twenty20 series against England. The mercurial 38-year-old, who had not played a Test since 2017, called time on his one-day career last year but kept the door open for T20s. He has not been picked since the World Cup in Sri Lanka in February, with selectors bypassing him for a series against Bangladesh in June. Maxwell was again overlooked for the squad named Monday to play England in November, with a host of younger players instead preferred. “A little bit sad and a little bit inevitable too, but I’m announcing my retirement from international cricket,” Maxwell said on the Final Word podcast. “We probably had numerous discussions before and after the T20 World Cup,” he added of talks with selectors. “And it was pretty open-ended. “There wasn’t any pressure from (Australia team management), and we decided to sort of leave the door open. “There was a couple of series that were coming up (in which) they were going to look to the future, and we saw that in Bangladesh with guys getting their opportunity and performing really well. “There was a small hope or discussion that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (against England). “But I can completely understand the direction they’re going with this squad.” Maxwell played 130 T20 internationals, blasting 2,897 runs with a strike rate of 154.42, leaving as Australia’s third-highest run-scorer after David Warner and Aaron Finch. While he only played seven Tests, he featured in 149 ODIs, crunching 3,990 runs. Maxwell also called time on his first-class career with Victoria, but will continue with the Melbourne Renegades in the Big Bash League. “I’m grateful for the time I was able to play for my country,” he said. “If you had offered me that career when I first walked into the Victoria change rooms in 2009-ish, I would have bitten your hand off.”

Indian national killed after 2 helicopters collide in Nepal's Mount Everest region. An Indian national was killed and a New Zealander injured after two helicopters collided as they prepared to land in Nepal’s Mount Everest region on Tuesday, authorities said. The New Zealander has been rescued, the chief district officer of Solukhumbu district, Kaman Singh Thapa Magar, told Reuters . The incident took place in the base camp area of Mount Everest, Magar said. The helicopters were operated by two private firms, Fishtail Air and Dynasty Air. Fishtail Air said in a statement that its helicopter was carrying passengers who had been rescued from the Everest region when it crashed while landing. The Indian and the New Zealander on board were tourists, a Fishtail official said, while a Dynasty Air official said its helicopter was carrying only cargo. The accident comes during the peak trekking season in Nepal, when helicopters ferry hikers and climbers in the region. Last week, six people were killed in a helicopter crash in the Indian Himalayan state of Uttarakhand. The helicopter was flying from Badrinath, a prominent pilgrimage destination for Hindus located in the mountains, to Dehradun city, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) said in a statement. All six people on board the chopper, including five passengers and the pilot, were killed, ANI reported, citing UCADA’s Chief Executive Officer Prateek Jain.

Is Rahul Gandhi ambitious?. MILLIONS of Indians evidently see Rahul Gandhi as their candidate to steer the country out of its deep mess driven by hate-filled divisive politics and a K-shaped economic trajectory plying unprecedented inequality. That seemed to be the unspoken sentiment, if not consensus, at the massive Sunday rally of opposition parties in Delhi against vote theft. The issue has brought out angry youth on the streets. Rigging of polls betrays, however, an inability to secure popular support through clean elections, which is a blessing. India is not alone in subverting democracy. Narendra Modi’s ride-or-die friendship with Benjamin Netanyahu reveals a shared scorn for secular democracy and minority rights. Netanyahu hopes to disenfranchise Palestinian MPs (strategically called Arabs by a clever political fiat) even as they mock him in turn by holding the balance of power, principally against him, after last week’s elections. Likewise with Modi, whose controversial victories in Bihar and West Bengal recently benefited enormously as his handpicked election commission disenfranchised millions of Muslim voters and other potential opponents of the regime. Netanyahu rewarded Modi’s friendship by giving his government the Pegasus spyware among other contraptions to undermine democracy. One would readily go along with the view that Gandhi makes for a great candidate to don the mantle of prime minister and also restore its prestige. He has displayed the drive to nurse Indian democracy back to health. But is he as equipped as, say, streetfighters like Priyank Kharge or M.K. Stalin or Akhilesh Yadav to deal frontally with the push which will inevitably arrive in the process of dismantling entrenched fascism? That Sonia Gandhi and both her children — Rahul as the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, Priyanka Gandhi as an outspoken and gritty parliamentarian — called out Israel’s genocide in Gaza, while major parties other than the left looked away is cause to celebrate the family — and also something to worry about as it puts them in the crosshairs of many a foreign and domestic interloper. The fact that the RSS chief hosted an Israeli diplomat as chief guest at the Hindutva body’s annual day on Dussehra is troubling. Has anyone bothered to ask Rahul Gandhi if he was himself interested in the job that so many appear keen to award him? A pivotal question needs to be flagged here about widespread faux expertise over a future prime minister from the opposition. Has anyone bothered to ask Rahul Gandhi if he was himself interested in the job that so many appear keen to award him? A fair guess based on history and Nehru-Gandhi genealogy is that Rahul Gandhi harbours no such ambitions. We could perhaps glean the truth of this hunch from Sonia Gandhi’s soon-to-be released memoirs. The BJP routinely accuses Jawaharlal Nehru and his daughter of political ambition. No Indian prime minister with a clear majority in parliament has offered to resign other than Nehru. In February 1950, Nehru offered to resign as prime minister over the refugee crisis after Partition. Sardar Patel persuaded him to withdraw the offer. Again, in 1958, Nehru announced his desire to step down and take a break from office, citing severe mental fatigue, fading idealism, and deteriorating public standards in Indian politics. A public outcry broke out, and the Congress begged him to stay on. Did Nehru want his daughter to succeed him? On the contrary, there’s plenty of evidence that he desired young socialist leader Jai Prakash Narayan as his deputy in 1952, which JP refused. There was not even a remote hint that he wanted his daughter in his cabinet or to succeed him. Nehru was wary of Morarji Desai from the right-wing of the party. He engineered a plan for senior cabinet ministers to resign to work at the grassroots with the party. He inducted Lal Bahadur Shastri as a minister without portfolio in the prime minister’s office, a clear signal who he was tapping as successor. Shastri’s demise in Tashkent set off another round of worry about Desai manoeuvring. Powerful regional satraps countered the move and promoted Indira Gandhi believing she could be manipulated. Mrs Gandhi favoured supporting Gulzari Lal Nanda. The ‘Syndicate’ supporting her was essentially conservative, pro-business, and staunchly anti-socialist. Mrs Gandhi turned the tables on them in 1969 by staging a split with the support of the communist bloc. When the left abandoned her after the emergency — one of their defining errors — she was swamped by the conservatives including religious revivalists who were largely seen as devising her fateful Punjab policy that would eventually lay her low. Rajiv Gandhi was a scrupulously private family man until Sanjay Gandhi’s death in a plane crash required him to stand with his mother. Her assassination set him up as prime minister. There’s no dearth of recorded evidence of Sonia Gandhi opposing his entry into politics. In an emotional showdown, she forbade him from becoming prime minister, presciently fearing he, too, would be killed. Rajiv’s response was: “I am her son … if I don’t do it, who will?” Ambition? Did Sonia Gandhi try to be prime minister in 1999 when she met the president with a list of 272 supporters? The world knows that she backed Manmohan Singh as prime minister in 2004. But a 2014 book by R.D. Pradhan, a civil servant close to Rajiv and Sonia Gandhi, described how Sonia Gandhi had Manmohan Singh in mind as early as 1999. On her part, Sonia Gandhi did one better. She set up a very effective advisory council to informally but crucially advise the Singh government on progressive issues ranging from poverty alleviation, right to information, right to education, halting disinvestment in public sector undertakings — everything that Nehru and Indira Gandhi would approve of. Rahul Gandhi would in all likelihood follow the precepts. His politically correct upbringing could struggle against the ugliness of right-wing politics that prompted Nehru to offer to resign. There are many more roughly hewn leaders in the progressive pack to confront an ugly pushback that would come from a cornered fascist order. The writer is Dawn’s correspondent in Delhi. jawednaqvi@gmail.com Published in Dawn, November 3rd, 2026

2 policemen martyred, 1 injured in attack en route to polio duty in KP's Mohmand. MOHMAND/TANK: Two policemen were martyred and another was injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire on them while they were on their way to join a polio team for security duty during the ongoing vaccination campaign in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Mohmand district on Tuesday, police said. Headquarters Deputy Superintendent of Police Liaquat Ali confirmed these details to Dawn , adding that the attack took place near the Hashim Kor police checkpost in the Dag Tamanzai area of the Pindiali tehsil. He identified the martyred cops as Constables Zahoor Khan and Arbai Khan and the injured policeman as Sepoy Sabir Khan. Later in the day, funeral prayers for the two martyred policemen were offered at the Police Lines in Ghalanai. The funeral was attended by the Commandant Mohmand Rifles, the deputy commissioner, the district police officer and other officials, as well as local residents. Senior officials laid floral wreaths on the bodies of the martyred policemen and offered condolences to their bereaved families. They also paid tribute to the sacrifices of the policemen. Separately, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi took notice of reports about the abduction of four polio workers in the province’s Tank district and directed relevant authorities to take “immediate and effective measures” for their safe recovery. Police say the incident took place on Monday. Governor Kundi termed the incident “extremely regrettable and condemnable”, a statement issued by his office on Tuesday said. The governor noted that polio workers “perform a national duty to protect children and promote a healthy Pakistan” and said the government was responsible for providing security to polio teams. He added that targeting polio workers was “against humanity and the national interest”. The incidents come as a sub-national polio vaccination campaign began across the country on Sunday, targeting nearly 24 million children in 97 high-risk districts. Pakistan and Afghanistan are the only two countries where polio is still endemic. On Sunday, Pakistan reported its eighth polio case of the ongoing year. The affected child was a 13-month-old girl from KP’s Khyber district. Of the eight cases, six have been reported from KP — including four from Bannu division — and two from Sindh. In July, Pakistan told the global Independent Monitoring Board that the country had entered a decisive phase in its decades-long fight against polio, claiming the virus had been pushed into a shrinking number of high-risk areas and cautioning that persistent insecurity, particularly in southern KP, remained the biggest obstacle to reaching every child. In September, two policemen were martyred as armed assailants fired at a polio vaccination team in Balochistan’s Noshki. Similarly, a police constable was martyred and four others were injured in an attack on a law enforcement party en route to provide security for polio teams in KP’s Hangu in April.

Respect for a woman’s dignity not just a matter of personal morality but constitutional obligation: Supreme Court. ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) stated on Tuesday that respect for a woman’s dignity was not merely a matter of personal morality but a constitutional obligation the state expected of everyone in its service. The declaration came as a two-member bench, headed by Justice Ayesha Malik and including Justice Shahid Waheed, rejected a plea filed by a former employee of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) against his compulsory retirement over the allegation that he had set his wife on fire. “Off-duty conduct of sufficient gravity may constitute misconduct and acquittal in a criminal case does not undo misconduct independently established in departmental proceedings,” affirmed Justice Shahid Waheed in the nine-page judgement authored by him. The plea was filed by Jawad Abbasi, who used to work as a cook in the IB, against a Jan 15 decision by the Federal Service Tribunal’s (FST) to uphold his compulsory retirement from service. He had faced disciplinary proceedings under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020 over allegations that he had set his wife on fire and was ill-mannered and short-tempered. Abbasi was also accused of conduct that was criminal, unprofessional and prejudicial to good order and service discipline. Moreover, his conduct was said to have adversely affected the reputation and discipline of the IB. The departmental proceedings found the charges established, and by an order dated June 14, 2024, he was penalised with compulsory retirement. His departmental appeal in the case had also been rejected, and his appeal pertaining to his service had been dismissed by the FST. However, lower court acquitted him in the criminal case in the matter. Before the SC, his counsel Aftab Alam Yasir argued that the matter at hand was a private and domestic one between the married couple, had no connection with the petitioner’s official duties, and that Abbasi’s conduct outside his workplace and office hours could not constitute misconduct under the Civil Servants Rules. The counsel pointed out that his client had previously been acquitted by a trial court, further claiming that his wife had attempted suicide. He contended that the rejection of Abbasi’s plea following the departmental inquiry was erroneous. In his judgement on the matter, Justice Waheed observed that the dignity of a woman, whether as a wife, sister, daughter, mother or a fellow citizen, was a fundamental value protected by the Constitution. “Respect for that dignity is not merely a matter of personal morality; it is an obligation that the state is entitled to expect from every person in its service,” the judgement said. It added that the conduct of a civil servant was not judged exclusively by the manner in which he performed his official duties. His character, integrity and conduct in private life may also become relevant where these factors bore upon his suitability to hold a public office, the discipline of the service or public confidence in the institution he served, Justice Waheed emphasised. A person’s conduct towards those within his own home may, in appropriate circumstances, reveal qualities of character that could not be disregarded merely because the conduct occurred beyond the workplace, the judgement said. “The walls of a home are not a jurisdictional boundary, and violence does not become private because it is committed behind a closed door,” Justice Waheed stated, adding that “fire does not become a family affair because it was lit indoors”. “The allegation is not of a quarrel or a harsh word. It is that the petitioner set his wife on fire, an act which, if established, is among the gravest forms of violence one person can inflict upon another,” the judgement said. It further stated: “It is no incident of married life; it is an assault on life and the dignity of a human being.” The court also observed that the first information report (FIR) in the case was registered under Section 324 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), which carried the penalty for an attempt to murder, and that burn injuries to the woman independently attracted the provisions on hurt in Chapter XVI (offences affecting the human body) of the PPC. The legislature had classified such conduct as a public wrong against the state, not a private dispute to be settled between spouses, the judgement said, adding that the right to life under Article 9 of the Constitution and the inviolability of the dignity of a person under Article 14 protected a wife within her home as fully as any citizen in a public place. “The Constitution does not stop at the threshold of a home; it walks in with every woman who lives there,” the judgement said. Moreover, Article 25(3) permitted special provision for the protection of women, and the legislature had acted upon it through, among other enactments, the Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2016 and the Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2020 for the Islamabad Capital Territory, the court observed. In addition, Pakistan was a party to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women , under which violence against women was recognised as a form of discrimination that the state must act to eliminate, the judgement said. “The burning of women in their homes, frequently passed off as a kitchen or stove accident or as attempted suicide, is a grave and recurring social evil in this country,” stated Justice Waheed. “The plea of suicide is often the final injury inflicted upon a burnt woman; having been robbed of her safety, she is then robbed of the truth, and her suffering is recast as her own doing,” he said in the judgement, adding that a public institution could not remain unconcerned about such an allegation against one of its own employees and that indifference would be a failure of institutional duty, not a mark of respect for privacy. “Conduct of this gravity bears directly on the petitioner’s suitability for public service. A civil servant found, on proper inquiry, to have used potentially lethal violence against his own spouse displays a want of self-control and a disregard for human life,” the court declared. It observed that such conduct was “wholly unbecoming” of a government servant and prejudicial to good order and service discipline. “Where he then seeks to escape responsibility by casting the blame upon the victim, claiming that she set herself alight, he adds deceit to violence. A man who sets his wife on fire and then calls it her suicide has failed twice, first as a husband and then as a witness to the truth; such a man cannot be called a gentleman,” the court ruled. The judgement said public confidence in the civil service rested on the assurance that those who served the state respected the dignity of those around them and a civil servant who denied that respect to his own wife forfeited the trust on which his office depended. “Public service is a trust, and the conduct of those who hold it is a matter of public concern, at home as much as at work,” the judgement said. “Respect for women is not a private virtue that a civil servant may practise or neglect as he pleases; it is part of the character [of] the state.”

Foreign women rape case: Incomplete police report clears five suspects of sexual assault charges. LAHORE: An incomplete investigation report (challan) filed before a trial court in connection with the alleged gang rape of two foreign women in July cleared five suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, of sexual assault charges. However, the report implicated them in other offences, including illegal detention and extortion. The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women. Defence C police registered the first information report (FIR) under Sections 365-A (kidnapping or abducting for extorting property, valuable security), 375-A (rape), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence), 368 (wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person) and 337-L (II) (punishment for other hurt) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) in July. The investigation report said the two complainants alleged that they had met one of the three prime suspects in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business. After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested a further $500,000. However, according to the police report, the women did not pay him any profits or return his investment this time. In June this year, the suspect invited the foreign women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to Murree and other areas. The investigation report alleged that the suspect subsequently told an associate that the women owed him money. The associate then involved another prime suspect, identified as “boss”. On June 29, the women were taken to a house in Defence Phase VII, Lahore, where they were allegedly detained and pressured to pay the amount. Police said the women were forced to transfer around $19,500, which was converted into rupees through a Lahore-based account. Of this amount, Rs1.1 million each reportedly went to two of the suspects. According to the report submitted to the court, the women alleged that armed men guarded them at the house, threatened them with a knife, a gun and a piece of broken mirror, and warned that they would be killed and their body parts sold if they failed to meet the demands. The report said the complainants’ statements and the investigation indicated that three suspects had committed sexual assault. Police said they found no evidence of rape against the other five suspects, including the relative of the political figure and the suspect identified as “boss”. The report further stated that the women escaped on July 1 when a car taking them to the airport met with an accident near Bhatta Chowk. They raised an alarm, following which the relative of the senior political figure fled, and the police took the women into their protection. Police also claimed to have recovered Rs4.3 million allegedly extorted from the women, along with a mobile phone and a vehicle allegedly used in the crime. Pistols and a rifle were also recovered, leading to the registration of separate cases under the Arms Ordinance, the report added. Another suspect was accused of renting the house to the group without informing the authorities, while a further suspect was allegedly involved in helping to destroy evidence. Sections 368 and 201 were added to the case on these grounds. Medical examinations of the complainants were conducted, and their statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were recorded before a magistrate. The incomplete investigation report further stated that DNA, fingerprint and polygraph tests had also been conducted, while call data records had been obtained. It added that the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s reports were still awaited. Therefore, the police submitted an incomplete investigation report to avoid delays, despite having sufficient evidence against the suspects. The police asked the court to summon the suspects through notices. Additional District and Sessions Judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal has already distributed copies of the police report among the suspects and fixed Nov 11 for the next hearing. Advocate Salman Shahid, defence counsel for two of the suspects charged with sexual assault, accused the police of favouring the key suspects in its investigation. He claimed that his clients were low-paid employees of one of the key suspects and had been made scapegoats. One of his clients was a member of the janitorial staff at the property where the alleged incident took place, he added. In July, Lahore Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Operations Faisal Kamran said that the police had been ordered to treat a suspect — reportedly linked to a senior government minister — in the case like “any other criminal”. DIG Kamran had recounted the events leading up to the recovery of the women and the subsequent arrest of the suspects in a press conference. He said that during the investigation it had emerged that a “criminal gang” may have been behind the incident. He further vowed that the police would ensure no legal loophole — which could be exploited in favour of the suspect — was left. The two women departed Pakistan on July 3.

Binance says outflows normalised as North Korea rejects US allegation over heist. Asset outflows from Binance have normalised and the company was in “very strong financial health”, its co-CEO said, as North Korea dismissed as “absurd rhetoric” US allegations that it was behind a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist on its platform. The world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, whose customers had withdrawn a net $4.72bn as of Monday after it was hit with what could be the largest-ever financial heist last week, has also launched a campaign to stem outflows and woo new users. “In the first 24 hours, there was a spike in terms of withdrawals, as can be expected. But after that … it’s pretty much normalised,” Richard Teng told a Hong Kong Fintech Week event on Tuesday. “The company is in very strong financial health,” he said, adding that 95 per cent of the affected tokens had been replenished. “This is something that we can cover. We are able to do so.” The crypto exchange was seeing “hourly deposits exceed withdrawals”, Binance said in an X post earlier on Tuesday, adding that it reflected improving user activity and stabilising flows. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on the weekend that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in crypto assets, a crime that sent shockwaves through the industry. Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said the US allegations proved Washington remained hostile towards Pyongyang, according to a report on Tuesday by state news agency KCNA . Pyongyang has not responded to US President Donald Trump’s overtures, made earlier this year, to resume summit diplomacy. In the wake of the US allegations, Kim Yo Jong said North Korea had “issues to reconsider” over what she called US hostility. “The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a ‘cyber criminal state,’ claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organisation ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” KCNA quoted Kim Yo Jong as saying. “But the US assertion is absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” said Kim, a ruling party official. DPRK is short for the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea. “It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds.” Revenue stream North Korea faces growing scrutiny over cryptocurrency theft , which analysts say is a key source of funds for its weapons programmes. Cybersecurity experts say North Korean hackers are among the world’s most prolific crypto thieves and the proceeds help fund the country’s efforts to develop nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles capable of hitting the United States. North Korea has stolen cryptocurrency worth $7.6bn this year, more than in any previous year, according to estimates by blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. North Korea denies allegations linking it to cryptocurrency theft and other cybercrimes. Analysts in Seoul said Pyongyang’s unusually swift response likely reflected concern that the allegation could lead to tighter efforts to disrupt revenue streams that North Korea is accused of using to finance its weapons. “With sanctions already in place, cryptocurrency theft has become one of North Korea’s key channels for securing funds for regime maintenance and weapons development,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies. Additional US measures targeting crypto wallets, laundering networks and cryptocurrency exchanges could choke off an important source of revenue, Lim said. South Korea’s central bank estimated North Korea’s gross domestic product at 47.18 trillion won ($35.09bn) in 2025, meaning the Binance theft could be equivalent to about a sixth of its economic output. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated 89pc of crypto hack losses in 2026 were linked to North Korea, up from 15pc in 2021. It said the average reported loss per hack rose from $50.65 million in 2021 to $185.65m in 2026. “I guess you could call it big game hunting, where they’re targeting these larger exchanges that may take more time and more complexity to be able to do … but the payoff can be relatively large,” said Alec Zebrick, senior manager of Asia-Pacific Global Services at Chainalysis. Infographic depicting amount lost every month due to crypto hacks. — Courtesy Reuters North Korea is one of the world’s most impoverished countries but has poured resources secured through illicit means and activities banned under UN Security Council resolutions into its missile and nuclear programmes. Kim Yo Jong said North Korea would “reconsider” unspecified issues in light of the “very unpleasant US hostile attitude”, without elaborating. North Korea has not publicly responded to Trump’s offers to resume summit diplomacy. Binance withdrawals Binance launched a campaign on Monday offering fee rebates, rewards to eligible users who rack up at least $10,000 in cumulative trading volume, as well as annual percentage rates of up to 10pc on certain yield-generating products. The exchange’s “community appreciation campaign” will run through November 21, a post on its website showed. Binance, which froze withdrawals for more than two days after the hack and then started allowing customers to withdraw again on Sunday morning in some assets, reopened withdrawals for more assets on Tuesday. Since the resumption of withdrawals, Binance has seen net outflows amounting to around 3pc of the assets on its platform, it said on Monday, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up. “The relatively contained price reaction suggests a degree of maturity and resilience,” said Maksym Repa, head of DeFi at Lombard, a Bitcoin finance protocol backed by Franklin Templeton. “Investors appear to be distinguishing between a security failure at a centralised exchange and a problem with the Bitcoin network itself.”

Petitions against detention of Sohail Afridi, others referred to PHC CJ for constitution of larger bench. PESHAWAR: A Peshawar High Court (PHC) bench on Tuesday referred multiple petitions challenging the detention of PTI leaders, including Sohail Afridi — the non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister — to the chief justice for the constitution of a larger bench. Afridi has not been seen since the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11. His whereabouts remained unknown on the day governor’s rule was imposed, and a federal minister confirmed a day later that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody . The PTI has also alleged the detention and arrests of several of its other members, including lawmakers and ministers. Their whereabouts have not been disclosed by the government so far. Multiple pleas have been filed in the PHC in this connection. A division bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali took up the petitions on Tuesday. Apart from Afridi’s detention, the petitions also pertain to the alleged disappearance of KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, MNAs Junaid Akbar and Dr Amjid Ali, provincial minister Amjid Ali Khan, MPAs Ikramullah and Aurangzeb Khan, former chief minister of Gilgit-Baltistan Mohammad Khalid Khursheed and several other PTI leaders. Afridi’s brother Mohammad Aamir filed one of the petitions, alleging that Afridi was “abducted” from Chief Minister House on the night that the emergency was imposed in the province. He had approached the PHC on Oct 13. On Tuesday, the bench referred the pleas to the chief justice after the KP government and senior police officials failed to file their respective replies in accordance with the court’s Oct 20 directives . “These are not ordinary personalities,” remarked Justice Ali during the hearing. Meanwhile, KP Advocate General Sanaullah Khan sought three days to submit the replies, adding that his office was awaiting a response from the provincial home department, police and other law enforcement agencies. Bashir Vazir, who appeared on behalf of the petitioners, alleged that the PTI leaders had been missing for many days. He contended that, under Article 199 of the Constitution, the PHC had authority to order that Afridi and Swati be produced before the court. He further argued that the KP Assembly had passed an immunity law under which a member of the assembly could not be arrested in such manner, adding that the assembly’s speaker also could not be arrested under the law. The law stipulated that the speaker would remain in office until a successor is elected, Vazir said. According to the KP advocate general, in more than 200 instances of detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO), orders were passed without the cases being heard. The bench disagreed with the claim, observing that in those cases reports had been sought from the respondents but were never submitted. It further observed that the detentions under consideration were not MPO cases. “This is an important case; the chief minister of the province is missing,” Justice Ali observed. The bench said the court had given the respondents 10 days to file replies, but they had not complied with the order. “We refer this case to the chief justice to constitute a larger bench,” Justice Ali said. The KP advocate general also requested the constitution of a larger bench.

IHC suspends order rejecting FIR plea in Pims fire case, seeks inquiry report and govt response. ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday suspended a Justice of the Peace’s order dismissing an application seeking the registration of an FIR into the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) neonatal fire tragedy . The court also directed the authorities to submit the complete record, along with the inquiry report, and issued notices to the respondents, including the federal government and the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The August 26 fire at a nursery in Pims’ Mother and Child Hospital claimed the lives of 14 newborns. The incident raised concerns over fire safety measures and sparked calls for accountability , with criminal action being ordered against eight officials . “I will call for all reports and summon all evidence,” Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro observed while hearing a petition filed by lawyer Riaz Hanif Rahi on behalf of The Jurists Foundation of Pakistan. “If any negligence comes to light, I will order the registration of a case against those responsible,” the judge added. The petition seeks the registration of an FIR in connection with the deaths of 14 newborns in a fire at the Gynaecology Ward/Special Care Centre of the Mother and Child Hospital (MCH) at Pims. The petitioner alleged that the incident was caused by gross negligence, including the absence of staff from a ward that had reportedly been locked to prevent theft. Earlier, on Aug 28, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered an inquiry against eight Pims officials over alleged negligence in addressing fire-safety deficiencies. The report alleged that the officials failed to take timely corrective measures despite being alerted to safety shortcomings, and that the subsequent tragedy could have been prevented. “In the Pims tragedy, 14 children were burned simultaneously,” he said, adding that “even among wild animals in the jungle, such a thing does not happen,” said the counsel. Justice Soomro, however, asked the counsel to restrict his submissions to the legal aspects of the case. When Rahi continued narrating details of the tragedy, the judge remarked: “You are veering off track again; please present legal arguments pertaining to your case.” The counsel argued that no FIR had been registered in the deaths to date. The judge asked whether an inquiry had been conducted. Rahi replied that the inquiry report had established negligence and urged the court to direct the registration of an FIR before the end of the court’s working hours. Explaining the delay, the counsel said the Justice of the Peace had dismissed his application on the grounds that petitions relating to the matter were already pending before the high court. He argued that, apart from him, no one else had approached the police station seeking the registration of a case and that an FIR should have been registered. “I have gathered so much evidence — but if an FIR is not registered, where am I supposed to take this evidence?” he asked. After hearing the arguments, the court suspended the Justice of the Peace’s order and directed the authorities to submit the complete record, including the inquiry reports, before the next hearing. It also directed that all evidence be placed on record. Other prayers The petition, filed under Article 199 of the Constitution, also seeks directions for the respondents to compensate the victims’ families under Section 323 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). It further asks the court to restrain government medical staff, including doctors, from engaging in private practice, particularly at commercial establishments, unless permitted under a validly framed law. Among other reliefs sought, the petitioner has asked the court to direct the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority to include individuals such as Dr Khaliq-uz-Zaman in its governing body, ensure that the relevant institutions meet ISO standards and direct the Auditor General to submit audit reports. In the event of any discrepancies, the petition seeks directions for the FIA to initiate proceedings. The petition also calls for the replacement of expired electrical wiring in government hospitals. It further seeks a declaration that placing newborns in isolation is unreasonable, illogical and illegal, and runs counter to maternal love. It further asks the court to declare the construction of the Mother and Child Hospital an encroachment on the hospital’s already approved plan and direct that the neonatal units be reconfigured so newborns can be placed within sight of their mothers and close to their beds. The petitioner has also sought compensatory costs for filing the public interest litigation. The court issued notices to the federal government through the Cabinet secretary, the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Interior, the Establishment Division, the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council, the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, the Auditor General of Pakistan, the Islamabad chief commissioner and deputy commissioner, the Capital Development Authority, Capital Emergency Services, the executive director of Pims, the Islamabad inspector general of police, the SSP Operations, the FIA director general and other respondents, seeking their replies. The hearing was adjourned until Nov 12.

French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer. France has opened a judicial investigation into a war crimes complaint over an Israeli strike on a residential building in Lebanon, a lawyer told AFP on Tuesday. French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri, whose parents were killed in the Beirut strike in 2024, filed the complaint as a civil party this year with the International Federation for Human Rights, Cherri’s lawyer Clemence Bectarte explained. The crimes against humanity unit of the Paris Judicial Court has appointed two investigating judges to the case, she added, hailing the move as “a first”. Hezbollah fought with Israel at the start of the war on Gaza following the events of October 7, 2023. The hostilities, which escalated into open war in September 2024, have left more than 4,000 dead in Lebanon and forced more than a million people to flee. Seven civilians, including Cherri’s father and mother, aged 87 and 77, were killed in the bombing of their 12-storey apartment building in central Beirut on November 26, 2024, according to the complaint seen by AFP . Three floors were destroyed. The strike occurred “just a few hours before the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah came into effect,” the complaint stated, citing detailed research by Amnesty International and Forensic Architecture into the incident. AFP has reached out to the Israeli military for comment. Cherri told AFP he had taken legal action “for the dignity of all civilian victims”. “For nearly two years, I have been fighting… to ensure that the Israeli bombing that killed my parents and five other civilians does not go unpunished,” he said. “What happened to my parents is not an isolated case… I hope this investigation will help break the impunity enjoyed by Israeli officials responsible for attacks against civilians in Lebanon and Palestine,” he added. Several investigations underway While the judicial investigation marks a first over alleged war crimes by Israeli forces in Lebanon, other cases are pending. French-Lebanese man Mohamad H., represented by lawyer Emmanuel Daoud, has sought action after losing his mother, sister, and two nephews in strikes on the southern city of Tyre during the night of April 16-17. In another case, a French entrepreneur born in Lebanon has accused the Israeli army of uprooting 600-century-old olive trees belonging to his family in a village in southern Lebanon. France’s National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT), which handles war crimes, has opened an investigation into allegations of torture and war crimes related to the Israeli forces’ interception of humanitarian flotillas bound for Gaza in 2025 and 2026. The PNAT also asked a Paris judge to open a war crimes investigation into the deaths of two French children in an Israeli bombing in Gaza in October 2023, while ruling out charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, according to sources close to the case.

IHC grants protective bail to TikToker booked following stampede at wedding event. ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, alias “Mr Pattlo”, after a stampede at his mehndi (henna) event in Sialkot claimed two lives. Jatt had announced holding a mehndi event and prize-distribution ceremony at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road on Friday night; however, with hundreds gathered at the site, a stampede occurred when the stadium gates opened, killing two and injuring 18 people. Subsequently, a first information report (FIR) was registered on October 31 at the Motra Police Station, naming Jatt, his brother, the owner of Faraz Cricket Ground, six others, and 40-45 unidentified security guards. On Tuesday, IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar approved the protective — also known as transitory — bail for the TikToker until Nov 10, allowing him to avoid arrest while he approaches the relevant court to seek legal remedy. He surrendered before the court in a wheelchair. Jatt had filed a petition, seeking the court’s intervention to prevent his arrest before he could reach the court of competent jurisdiction. Advocates Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi and Barrister Raja Ali Abbas Jalap filed the petition on his behalf. According to the legal document, Jatt was named in the FIR, which was registered under Sections 322 (punishment for qatl-i-khata ), 440 (mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt), 431 (mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 149 (unlawful assembly), 188 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant) and 109 (punishment of abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), read with Section 16 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960. During the proceedings, the petitioner’s counsel argued that the FIR was registered outside the IHC’s territorial jurisdiction. However, the counsel maintained that the sole object of seeking protective bail was to enable a suspect present within the jurisdiction of one court to safely approach the court where the case was registered without being arrested on the way. “The merits of the case are not required to be examined at this stage,” the petition stated, adding that without the protection, the petitioner’s right to seek pre-arrest bail before a Sialkot court would be rendered illusory. The petition further contended that the allegations levelled against the petitioner were “false, frivolous, and baseless,” claiming that he had been falsely implicated. It was also brought to the court’s notice that the petitioner had no previous criminal record and that no other petition seeking the same relief had been filed before any other court. After hearing the arguments, Justice Dogar granted the relief, noting the temporary and limited nature of the protective bail and allowing the petitioner time to surrender before the appropriate forum. On Sunday, Sialkot police said they had arrested six suspects in relation to the incident. Police said Jatt immediately fled the scene after the incident, adding that their investigation and raid teams were conducting operations to apprehend the TikTok influencer. Sialkot District Police Officer Dost Muhammad confirmed that the six arrested individuals were involved in managing the event. According to the DPO, organisers had invited a large number of people by advertising a lucky draw featuring prizes such as motorcycles, a car and other valuable items via social media. During the event, an announcement was made over the loudspeakers instructing all attendees to enter the grounds simultaneously. This simultaneous entry into the sports stadium triggered a severe stampede, the DPO said. He stated that the organisers violated the terms of their permit, as well as established safety standard operating procedures (SOPs). The stampede also disrupted the flow of traffic on the main Daska-Sialkot Road. The Sialkot DPO declared that legal action would be taken against all those responsible for the incident, without any discrimination.

Lahore court grants NCCIA further two-day remand of suspects over US postage stamp fraud. LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) a further two-day physical remand of two suspects in a Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps. The prime suspect, identified as a 33-year-old resident of Khanewal, had been charged by a Florida jury with defrauding the United States Postal Service (USPS) of $126 million, the US Attorney’s Office of the Southern District of Florida said on Sept 28. The Lahore NCCIA announced the prime suspect’s arrest in late October, and he was sent on a five-day physical remand on Oct 21. Today’s extension of the physical remand is the third for him, and second for the co-suspect . On Tuesday, the NCCIA produced both men before Judicial Magistrate Naeem Wattoo upon the expiry of their latest four-day remand . The investigating officer (IO) sought custody of the suspects for another five days for interrogation. However, Magistrate Wattoo granted the agency two more days of physical custody and directed the IO to produce the suspects again on Nov 5. According to NCCIA, the initial investigation revealed that the prime suspect operated a website to market and sell over 5m fake US postage stamps over a period of more than three years. According to the US Department of Justice, the website run by the Pakistani national was not authorised to sell USPS products and services. The counterfeit labels allegedly allowed customers to ship packages at rates “far below legitimate USPS prices”, it said, adding that it caused losses exceeding $126m to the postal service. US prosecutors alleged that the website sold the labels for around $2 each, regardless of a package’s weight, size or destination. A US court order authorised the seizure and shutdown of the website. Money trail In a press conference on Oct 20, NCCIA’s Lahore Zone Additional Director Atif Ameer said that 16 bank accounts had been used in the scam. Seven of the accounts were operated by the suspect, five by his brother, two by his wife, and one each by his sister and aunt. He said the agency had expanded the investigation across several parts of the country. “Eight special teams were formed in Punjab, Islamabad and Sindh to trace the suspect and investigate the network,” he said and added the teams conducted raids at 35 locations and questioned 47 people as part of the investigation. “Investigators also employed digital and forensic techniques to establish the suspect’s movements and identify people associated with the operation.” Ameer added that investigators analysed 122 call-data records, 50 IMEI-tracking reports and audio and video recordings from 120 cameras. “Artificial intelligence and other modern technological tools were also used during the investigation. A locator operation continued for 10 days as investigators attempted to establish the suspect’s whereabouts and trace his activities,” he said. The NCCIA said the major focus of the investigation was the financial trail generated by the online sale of the counterfeit stamps. “We are examining transactions conducted through the 16 bank accounts and attempting to determine the flow of funds between the accounts allegedly belonging to the suspect and his relatives. “The involvement of family members is also being examined as part of the investigation, particularly the alleged use of their bank accounts in connection with the online business,” the additional director said. He said the role of other individuals in operating the website, processing orders, receiving payments or distributing the counterfeit stamps was also being probed. “Investigators are also working to establish the full scale of the operation and verify the volume and value of the transactions,” he said.

Soaring LPG prices force rickshaw drivers in Pakistan to cut meals. For 13 years, Rashid Ali has driven a three-wheeled motorised rickshaw around Lahore. His day starts at 6am and sometimes does not end until midnight, but he was long able to make around Rs1,700 ($6.50) a day, enough for his family’s bare essentials. Now, with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surging, he doesn’t even make half that. Ali, 33, is among thousands of drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly used for cooking and heating. Rashid Ali waits for customers while offering rides in his liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)-powered auto-rickshaw along a road in Lahore, on October 30, 2026. — Reuters Majeed Ghauri, Chairman of the Awami Rickshaw Union, calls it “the fuel of the poor” and says about 70 per cent of its members’ 43,000 auto-rickshaws and nearly 8,000 Qingqi motorcycle-based three-wheelers, which carry several passengers on set routes, run on LPG. LPG prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed , halting imports, traders say, in the latest energy shock since the US-Iran war began in February. One of the border crossings was opened a week later. With Ali now lucky to make around Rs800 ($3) a day, his family has cut back on meals, eating only twice a day. “Previously, when LPG was cheap, we could earn a decent income,” Ali said. “Now, it’s just not possible to get by on Rs700 or Rs800, is it?” A man fills a cylinder with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) at his shop in Lahore on October 30, 2026. — Reuters Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said. Traders said the price of a 12-kilogramme cylinder jumped 56pc within days of the closure to Rs7,000, or about Rs583 rupees per kg in the open market. Walking away Ali pays Rs600 a day to rent his rickshaw, filling up with fuel four or five times a day, at Rs300 to Rs400 a time. As well as daily expenses, Ali also pays Rs11,000 a month for his home and has two young children to support. Adding to his problems, passengers, he said, do not want to pay higher fares. “For a trip that should cost Rs200 or Rs250, they might only offer Rs80, Rs100, or Rs150 rupees,” Ali said. Passenger Mohammad Ramzan said when a driver asked Rs500 rupees for a ride in the city, he offered half that. When the driver declined, he walked away, he said. Inflation hit 9.6pc in October and the central bank last week raised interest rates to 12pc, citing energy and wheat prices. Petrol hit a record Rs458 a litre on April 3 and remains about 40pc above its pre-war price. Back home at midday, Ali said his two boys still needed their lunch. He would go out again until late at night, he said, hoping to make enough to bring something for the children to eat at night. Rashid Ali is reflected in a side mirror as he drives his liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)-powered auto-rickshaw along a road in Lahore on October 30, 2026. — Reuters

Entertainer and enigma, Glenn Maxwell bows out as cricket's great what-if. Part entertainer, part enigma, Glenn Maxwell will go down in cricket folklore as the game’s great what-if a maverick shot-maker whose limited-overs wizardry never extended to red-ball cricket. Where many of his peers stuck to the batting manual, Maxwell rewrote it with his 360-degree stroke-play, which made field settings a nightmare for rival captains. It could not be risk-free, but Maxwell cared little as he pulled off reverse hits and cheeky scoops with a gum-chewing nonchalance. Fans expected spectacle whenever Maxwell walked out with the bat and, more often than not, he delivered it with his unorthodox shots. The definitive example came at the 2023 ODI World Cup. Chasing 292 against Afghanistan and with Australia reeling at 91-7, Maxwell conjured up an unforgettable 201 not out off 128 balls to complete a chase that had looked impossible. That sense of occasion was present from his Australia debut, an ODI against Afghanistan in 2012, and it studded his career. A two-time ODI World Cup winner, Maxwell also hit the winning runs in Australia’s maiden T20 World Cup triumph in 2021 under captain Aaron Finch. Fittingly, Finch fronted the tributes to Maxwell after a 286-match international career spanning 14 years. “Without doubt one of the most destructive players the game has ever seen and easily one of the most innovative of our generation,” Finch wrote on Instagram. “Some of the things you’ve done on a cricket field have been absolutely ridiculous. You’ve played innings that most of us could only dream of and produced some of the greatest moments this game has ever seen. You’ve changed the way the game is played and inspired so many along the way.” T20 royalty Maxwell’s value was always three-dimensional: explosive batting, savvy off-spin, and electric fielding that saved runs and snared jaw-dropping catches. It made him T20 royalty, especially in the Indian Premier League (IPL). Maxwell, 38, was an IPL millionaire at 25 and earned the nickname the “Big Show” after his first ODI series a moniker he resented. “At the start, I thought if I fight it, I’m going to have to live with it even more, so I tried to sort of ride with it,” Maxwell said in 2014. “I’m just trying to shake it off because it’s starting to go too far. “It’s not about what I’m about. I’m all about trying to entertain and…I just love being out there trying to hit balls for four and six.” That ability made him a crowd magnet evident in his 12.4 million followers across social media platforms. The long run was not without quiet chapters, and test cricket never became his stage. Maxwell played only seven tests between 2013 and 2017, scoring 339 runs at a modest average of 26. He took a mental health break from the sport in 2019 and recounts the episode in his autobiography in a candid assessment of the struggles that lay beneath his confident exterior.

JI and Dar hold 'candid discussions' on fuel relief, agree to continue talks in coming days. The government and Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) on Tuesday held “candid discussions” on practical measures to provide relief to low-income citizens in petroleum prices. After a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif last week, both sides agreed to form a bipartisan committee to expand the government’s ongoing fuel relief scheme in response to JI’s demands for the abolition of the petroleum levy. JI also warned of resuming its postponed march to Islamabad by mid-November if no relief was announced. Subsequently, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday held a meeting with a JI delegation, led by its Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch, to discuss petroleum prices in the country, according to the Dar-led Foreign Office (FO). “The two sides held candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens,” the FO statement said. Both sides agreed to continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief, it added. During the meeting, DPM Dar reiterated the “government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges”, the statement said. He also emphasised that “sustained cross-party dialogue” remained key to addressing national economic challenges “effectively”. According to the statement, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Adviser to Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the finance secretary, and the Petroleum Division’s special secretary also attended the meeting from the government’s side. JI claims agreement on inclusion of 1,000cc cars in scheme After the meeting with the government’s team, the JI vice emir also addressed a press conference in Islamabad, according to a press release issued by the party. During his address, Baloch said that negotiations between the government and JI over the abolition of the petroleum levy and provision of relief to the public had entered their final stage. “Both sides have acknowledged that abolishing the petroleum levy is essential, while the government has also agreed to provide relief to the agricultural sector and owners of vehicles up to 1,000cc,” Baloch claimed. The ongoing relief scheme for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc was rolled out across the country on Sept 17. PM Shehbaz had announced the subsidies to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation. While describing the meeting as the final round of negotiations, Baloch said representatives of both sides will meet again tomorrow to discuss further progress. He said JI had presented six proposals to the government to provide relief to the people. “These included abolishing the petroleum levy, introducing a relief package, reducing public transport costs and extending relief to owners of vehicles above 800cc and the agricultural sector,” he said, noting that four key points were discussed today. The JI vice emir said both negotiating teams would prepare working papers on the gradual elimination of the levy and measures to provide relief to the public. “The government will complete its working paper today, while representatives of both sides will meet again tomorrow to discuss further progress,” Baloch said. He added that JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman would also review the draft agreement before announcing the party’s future course of action. He further disclosed that he had spoken by telephone with Rehman, who is currently in Turkiye, and briefed him on the progress of negotiations and sought his guidance. Baloch maintained that although the government had announced some relief measures, the ruling elite remained unwilling to surrender their privileges. He criticised the government for allowing oil refineries to earn excessive profits and said there was no solid justification for continuing the petroleum levy. Under a newly announced arrangement , oil refineries would contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a monthly cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price on consumers’ end. Baloch affirmed that JI’s primary objective was to secure relief for the people, contending that the government has taken various relief measures due to his party’s negotiations. He further said that upon his return from Turkiye, Rehman would address JI workers nationwide online and announce the party’s future strategy. “Our protests will continue, and we will also engage in negotiations because we want to secure relief for the people,” Baloch said. “If this package does not come in the form of public convenience and substantial relief, Jamaat-i-Islami will fulfil its commitment to the people, and in mid-November, our protest march will set off from Multan towards Islamabad,” Baloch declared. “Our stance is very clear and unequivocal; we will also exercise the right to protest, but our protest will be peaceful, dignified, and aimed at securing relief for the people, as always.” JI protests so far The JI has been demanding for over two months that the Centre abolish petroleum levies, as fuel prices have skyrocketed due to conflicts in the Middle East since March. The Centre and JI had agreed to form committees in early September — when the latter had planned a nationwide strike — to recommend measures to reduce the levy. On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government. On Sept 22, the JI emir said his party, whose convoy had reached Multan, was postponing its long march at the request of PM Shehbaz, who had assured the other side of a meeting to discuss the matter. When PM Shehbaz and Rehman finally met about a month later, they agreed to form a joint committee to recommend proposals for expanding the fuel relief scheme and for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy for the next budget.

CM Maryam incensed at Chaudhry Salik's claims of corruption in Punjab. LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday said she would be sending a defamation notice to Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain for levelling allegations of corruption against her government. During a private television channel talk show on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi. However, he also took a swipe at the present provincial administration, alleging that political considerations were increasingly shaping development priorities and influencing the allocation of public funds. He said he regularly heard complaints of corruption in Punjab, alleging that a disproportionate share of the province’s development budget was being channelled towards Lahore. Addressing a ceremony in Attock on Tuesday, CM Maryam said: “There is a federal minister … somebody sent me his statement about corruption in Punjab. Today, I am sending him a defamation notice.” She said that she would not hear “false allegations of corruption”. “If you have evidence, bring it forth — otherwise I will drag you to court,” she said. She also asked him why he remained a minister in a government that he considered corrupt. The chief minister went on to say that the reason behind the anger of the PML-Q leader was neither a matter of corruption nor progress. The issue, she said, was that she changed the deputy commissioner (DC) of Gujrat a few days ago whereas Salik had wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed. “I will not allow anyone to interfere in the will of the people,” she said. Maryam also took exception to Salik’s comments calling Elahi the “best-ever chief minister” in Punjab. “The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining. Believe me … the water was up to here,” she said, gesturing to her neck. “My Land Cruiser was completely submerged,” she said. “It looked less like Gujrat and more like a village … now, go and look at Gujrat. Now, when it rains, the rainwater doesn’t accumulate. That work was not done by the Chaudhrys,” she said. Speaking to the media in the wake of CM Maryam’s comments, Salik said he was sticking to his statement. In remarks aired by Geo News , he said: “God save us from pride and arrogance”. Asked about providing evidence for the corruption allegations, he said: “Please go and listen to the interview again.” He also refuted the claim that the row had to do with distracting from the matter of new provinces. “It was an interview, someone asked a question and I responded honestly,” he said. “Yes, there definitely is [corruption],” he added. Responding to the remarks, CM Maryam said: “So, levelling false accusations is considered humility, while offering a response is deemed arrogance? Bravo!” During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending , particularly the use of official aircraft , arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips. He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance. His comments had also prompted a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised the PML-Q leader not to “bite the hand that feeds him”. Bokhari had also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request for appointment of a DC of his choice being turned down. The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote. While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

Islamabad ATC grants bail to Imaan, Hadi in police altercation case. ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Tuesday granted bail to lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, in a case registered against them for allegedly blocking a road outside the National Press Club and engaging in an altercation with police. ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain announced the decision after hearing the bail applications. The police also produced the case record before the court during the proceedings. When defence counsel Riasat Ali Azad informed the court that the record had been received that day, the judge remarked that he would have shown the police the consequences of failing to produce it on Tuesday. The judge then asked the applicants if they had anything to say before announcing that their bail applications had been accepted. The court granted bail to both accused against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each. The judge also said he would examine the matter regarding the show-cause notice issued to the police over the delay in producing the case record. Last week, an ATC sentenced Imaan and Hadi to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case. The court also handed down one-year sentences and imposed fines of Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). They were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging his duty) of the PPC. Jailed, sentenced, re-arrested The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On September 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the SC suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with the security breach case. The case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency. Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House. Multiple polls predict Democrats will take control of the House of Representatives and have a shot at seizing the Senate on the back of voter resentment at a deeply unpopular president, soaring energy costs and the dragging conflict with Iran. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials. Voters cast their ballots inside a polling location in the social hall at St Patrick’s Church on November 3, 2026 in Youngstown, Ohio. — AFP The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war on Iran. All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands. Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans. In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff, who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future. “I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP . Economic discontent Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.
